title: Surge admission fencepost race causes tenant request shedding during regional failover
creator: Asha Patel
description: High-level summary: On 2026-03-09 23:40 UTC a subset of tenants (mainly low-throughput customers) experienced sustained 503/QUOTA_REJECT errors for ~18 minutes during a regional failover. The root symptom was a race in the surge-admission codepath: concurrent lease-table compaction + admission-window evaluation produced an off-by-one/fencepost miscount of available micro-credits, which caused the admission gate to refuse ephemeral slots for small tenants while allowing larger tenants to consume headroom. This manifested as silent shedding rather than clear throttling, which complicated detection and customer escalation. Impact: multiple mid-market customers reported service degradation and opened support tickets. We triggered a P0 response, issued mitigations and an emergency patch to the admission gate until a safe long-term fix is implemented.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate regional control-plane failover where scale-controller restarts quickly and re-registers 200+ reserved-pool leases in parallel.
Simulate a traffic profile with a mix of large sustained tenants and many small intermittent tenants hitting burst endpoints (tokenized short calls).
Trigger lease-table compaction in the same window as the admission evaluation (compact interval forced to 0s in test harness).
Observe surge_admission_rejections metric spike and 503s for small-tenant requests. Verify log lines: 'admission: available_micro_credits computed=0 expected>0 fencepost-check failed'.

root_cause: A race between the lease-table compaction routine and the surge admission evaluation produced a fencepost error in the available_micro_credits calculation. When compaction removed stale lease entries concurrently with admission evaluation, the admission code path could read an intermediate state that undercounted micro-credits by one or more for small tenants. Because admission decisions are taken per-request and not retried uniformly, this produced silent shedding concentrated on low-rate tenants during high churn (regional failover + coordinated re-registration). The immediate code path lacked an atomic snapshot or a versioned read, and assumptions about compaction being low-frequency were invalid during failover.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Emergency patch (PR #1287) deployed to canary and then region-wide: increase admission evaluation window and add conservative fallback that treats negative/zero micro-credit readings as 'degraded' rather than outright refusal. 2) Temporarily disabled lease-table compaction in the affected regions for 24h to avoid concurrent mutation during failover. 3) Added a monitoring alert on surge_admission_rejections > 50/min per region and an auto page to on-call.
long_term_fix: Implement atomic snapshot read for lease-table (version + epoch) so admission sees a consistent view even if compaction runs concurrently.
Replace ad-hoc micro-credit arithmetic with an explicit per-tenant atomic counter persisted to the lease store (schema migration required).
Add cross-region chaos testing to CI that forces simultaneous controller restarts + compaction to exercise race windows.
Introduce unit/integration tests that validate admission under corner cases (compaction+re-registration) and enforce invariants via property tests.
Design an admission simulator/tooling to model mixed-tenant workloads and produce headroom forecasts used by the autoscaler.
Plan staged rollout: canary (1 region, 5% traffic) -> regional (2 regions) -> global with health gating and automatic rollback on rejection regression.
acceptance_criteria: Admission path reads a versioned snapshot of the lease table under high churn; tests exercise the race and pass deterministically.
No unexplained surge_admission_rejections spikes in the regional canary during 72h soak under synthetic churn (target < 5/min).
Schema migration for per-tenant micro-credit counter completes without rolling restarts longer than 10s for any listener process.
CS confirms affected customers have stable traffic and no recurrence in their accounts for 7 days post-rollout.
qa_plan: Run race harness in CI with 'chaos' toggle enabled for admission+compaction path (target: 1000 parallel re-registrations).
Create end-to-end scenario in staging that mirrors failover pattern. Verify canary region for 72h with synthetic clients that mimic low-rate tenants.
Run smoke tests for dedicated pool latency/throughput after migration; ensure no regression in P95/P99 token latency beyond 5%.
Coordinate with SRE to run a controlled regional controller restart during a maintenance window after canary success.
customer_comms: We proactively notified affected customers on 2026-03-10, apologized, and issued one week of credits for impacted usage. CS/Sales follow-ups scheduled. A post-incident summary will be published to impacted customers with a technical explanation and mitigation timeline after the long-term fix is deployed.
notes: Telemetry: surge_admission_rejections metric rose from baseline ~2/min to 420/min at peak in region eu-west-1 during failover window.
Observed correlation with increased leader-election churn in scale-controller at 23:38 UTC (stack traces attached to PR #1293).
Hotfix approach chosen to reduce customer-impact window even though it is conservative and may slightly reduce aggregate burst throughput for short interval (~1-2%).
Risk: schema migration requires careful rollout to avoid coordination across num-worker processes. Migration runbook drafted in Confluence: /confluence/runtime/lease-counter-migration.
